actual.transcript:
Thanks for making time, both. The goal today is to get the security review moving again — it's been the blocker for three weeks.
Honest answer from our side: the review is stuck because we're missing two inputs — your completed SIG Lite questionnaire and evidence from a recent penetration test. Handling patient lab results, our infosec team can't wave either through.
The questionnaire is ninety percent done, our security lead has the last section. I'll send the completed SIG Lite questionnaire back to Freya by June 5th.
Friday works. If I have it Friday, I can start the internal review the following week.
And the pen test — we have the Q1 report from our external testers. Do you need the full report or a summary?
A summary with scope and findings severity is enough. Actually, easier if it lives with the rest of the evidence — I'll get the pen test summary uploaded to your portal by Monday, June 8th, once Sam shares it.
I'll email it to you right after this call, it's ready to go.
Then the last link in the chain is me. The warehouse team won't create the service account until security signs off — and with PHI in the schema they're strict about it.
Can we pre-agree the shape so it's a same-day job once you get the green light?
Yes — read-only, scoped to the ANALYTICS schema, key-pair auth. I'll provision the read-only Snowflake service account as soon as security signs off — targeting Wednesday, June 10th.
That's realistic if the questionnaire lands Friday.
Do we need your change advisory board for the account creation? That added two weeks last time at another customer.
No — we agreed internally last month that read-only analytics accounts skip the change board. It goes straight through.
Excellent. So: questionnaire Friday the 5th, pen test summary Monday the 8th, service account Wednesday the 10th. That's the chain unblocked.
Agreed. Nice to have dates on it at last.
Thanks all — I'll recap in the portal after this.

actual.transcript:
Great kickoff last week. This week is about getting the plumbing in so we can compile your project. First up: repo access.
Easy one. I'll get you the dbt repo access — invite to the quarry-integration GitHub team by tomorrow, July 3rd.
Perfect. Once I'm in, do we work off main or do you want us on a fork?
Off main, against the existing production target. A fork would just drift.
Agreed. Then on our side — I'll connect the warehouse and get the dbt project compiling in Quarry by Tuesday, July 7th.
That depends on network access though — our Redshift cluster only accepts whitelisted IPs.
Right, I'll send you our static IP ranges after this call. Can you get them whitelisted before Tuesday?
Yes — I'll whitelist Quarry's IPs on the Redshift cluster by Monday the 6th.
For context on urgency: our board meeting is end of July and I'd love the subscriber retention dashboard live for it.
That's a realistic target if the compile lands next week. We'll scope the retention dashboard properly at next Thursday's sync rather than promise it today.
Fair. Plumbing first.
So: repo invite tomorrow, IPs Monday, compile Tuesday. Speak Thursday.
Sounds good, thanks Maya.

actual.transcript:
Thanks for making time. I know this project has been stuck behind the security review, so I mostly want to understand where that stands.
Fair. It's taken longer than any of us wanted — the questionnaire touched teams that don't usually review vendors together, and anything touching patient data gets extra scrutiny.
Understood. Is there anything outstanding on our side? More documentation, a call with your reviewers?
No, your responses were complete, including the HIPAA and data-handling sections. The remaining answers are drafted internally and I'm waiting on one approval from our platform lead. I expect to close the review out early next week.
That's genuinely good news. Oliver, once that lands, what's the path to getting us connected?
The moment Nadia signs off, I'll provision the Snowflake service account — read-only on the ANALYTICS schema, exactly as specced. It's a same-day job once the review closes, so I won't put a separate date on it.
And just to confirm scope while we're all here: read-only, ANALYTICS schema only, no raw layer?
Correct. Our data governance policy won't allow raw-layer access for external tools — that's where the identifiable lab results live — and honestly you don't need it.
Agreed, we don't. Once the service account exists we can connect the dbt repo the same day, so the chain unblocks quickly.
That's what I'm hoping. We've lost about three weeks; if the connection happens next week we can claw most of that back.
From my side, no further reviews needed after this one. The tool itself was approved — it was the data-sharing terms for the health data that took time.
Good to know. I won't pile more actions on — the sign-off and the service account are the whole critical path. Anything you need from me?
Nothing right now. If provisioning throws anything weird I'll ping you on Slack.
Perfect. Let's speak once the account is live. Thanks both.

actual.transcript:
Morning both. Nadia, I'm hoping you have news on the security review.
I do — good news finally. We signed off the infosec questionnaire yesterday afternoon. That review is done from our side.
Fantastic. That's been the long pole for three weeks, so everything downstream can move now.
Which means the service account is on me next. What exactly do you need?
A read-only Snowflake service account scoped to the analytics schema — the de-identified marts, not the raw PHI — and our static IPs added to your network policy.
The IP allowlist goes through my team — send us the list and we'll process it with the sign-off paperwork.
Will do — I'll send over the Quarry static IP list by tomorrow so your team can add it to the network policy.
And I'll get the Snowflake service account created by Friday. Platform team has capacity this week.
Perfect. Once both land, we connect the warehouse and the repo the same day.
One thing to flag — our HIPAA audit season starts in August, so we may want to think about access reviews before then.
Noted, let's scope that once we're connected rather than now.
Fine by me. It was mostly a heads-up.
Great. So: questionnaire is done, IP list from me tomorrow, service account from Oliver by Friday. Real progress.
Feels good to be moving again. Thanks Sam.

actual.transcript:
Owen! Good to have you back — congratulations again.
Thanks Maya. Sorry the project went dark for three weeks, that was me, not the team losing interest.
No apology needed. Let's rebuild the picture — where do things actually stand?
Better than you'd think. IT finished the Okta SAML SSO configuration while I was out — it's done, tested, people log in through Okta now.
Excellent, I'll stop chasing that one. The other open item on my board is the metric definitions.
Yeah, that one's still on me and still not started. We still owe you the metric definitions — I'll get the first ten drafted in the yml now that I'm back.
Good. Given the gap, I don't want to pretend the old dates still hold.
Agreed, chasing the original timeline would just stress everyone out.
Then I'll re-baseline the implementation timeline and send you the updated plan by Thursday.
Perfect. One more thing from our side — your team asked what fields we track per shipment.
Yes, we need that to model the shipment marts properly.
I'll deliver the shipment data dictionary by end of next week — it exists, it just needs cleaning up before I share it.
That unblocks the modeling work nicely. Anything else in flight I should know about?
There's vague talk of a carrier-scorecard module on our roadmap that might want dashboards, but it's a quarter away at least.
Noted for later, not for the plan. Great to have you back, Owen.
Good to be back. Talk Thursday when the plan lands.
